classificationRule: Assign one primary bucket to each atomic observed fact. Record source, target, operation, outcome, severity, confidence, and causalEventId as separate fields. Split compound operations into linked events.

buckets.title: Source and dependency change
buckets.ownershipRule: A revision, file, manifest, lockfile, package, or tool input changes before building.

buckets.title: Build and test result
buckets.ownershipRule: A compiler, package, scanner, or test run reports its own result or artifact creation attempt.

buckets.title: Release and deployment transition
buckets.ownershipRule: A built artifact is promoted, deployed, installed, published, rolled back, or withdrawn.

buckets.title: Configuration and policy change
buckets.ownershipRule: A non-identity runtime setting, feature flag, rule, or operational policy changes.

buckets.title: Identity and authorization
buckets.ownershipRule: Authentication, session, account, role, permission, or access decision is observed.

buckets.title: Process and service lifecycle
buckets.ownershipRule: A process, worker, daemon, task, or local IPC endpoint starts, stops, or changes ownership.

buckets.title: Network and IPC activity
buckets.ownershipRule: A transport connection, DNS lookup, request, webhook, or endpoint exchange occurs or fails.

buckets.title: Data and storage lifecycle
buckets.ownershipRule: An application data record, file, object, archive, or backup is read, written, moved, retained, or deleted.

buckets.title: Security detection and finding
buckets.ownershipRule: An assessor or detector reports a vulnerability, suspicious behavior, secret exposure, or policy violation as a finding.

buckets.title: Health and recovery
buckets.ownershipRule: Runtime availability, resource exhaustion, crash, degraded state, failover, or restoration is observed.

tieBreaks.reason: The observed fact is the access decision; record the transport request separately only if needed.
A test result is not a runtime outage.
The observed fact is service health; a separate process exit may be linked as E06.
The promotion is E03; the worker start is a separate linked E06 event.

tieBreaks.case: source file written by application data workflow
tieBreaks.reason: Classify by role of the file in the observed operation, not its extension.
The finding is E09; an observed data transfer is a separate E07 or E08 event.
Permission transitions own this event even when implemented through cloud configuration.
The policy edit is E04; subsequent record deletion is separate E08.
